sections.h2: Where is the Wake County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office sits in the Wake County Justice Center at 300 S. Salisbury St., Suite 1700, Raleigh, NC 27601, and it is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The county lists 919-856-5460 and rodinfo@wake.gov for questions.

The county site describes the register as custodian and manager of a large number of public records, including deeds, deeds of trust and subdivision plats. It also issues marriage licenses and supplies copies of birth and death certificates.

If you are selling a Raleigh-area house, you will rarely visit in person. Closing attorneys normally file the deed for you, and the recording office is the last stop that makes your sale part of the public record.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed in Wake County cost?
sections.html:
A standard deed or other instrument costs $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each additional page, and a deed of trust costs $64 for the first 35 pages plus $4 per additional page. Those figures come from the register's own fee page.

Wake County Register of Deeds fee page, selected recording charges
Document or serviceFee as printed
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64 first 35 pages; $4 each additional page
Amendment to deed of trust$26 first 15 pages; $4 each additional page
All other documents and instruments$26 first 15 pages; $4 each additional page
Non-standard document$25 on top of the recording fee
Each extra instrument in one document$10
Satisfaction of a security instrumentFree
Map (plat) recording$21 per page
Certified copy$5 first page; $2 each additional page
Deed excise tax, August 1, 1991 to present$2 per thousand

The same page adds $2 for each party name beyond 20 on a document, and the first additional deed of trust reference on an assignment is free, with $10 for each reference after that.

sections.h2: What makes a deed standard or non-standard in Wake County?
sections.html:
A deed is standard only if it meets every item on the register's checklist; failing any one adds the $25 non-standard fee. The county lists the criteria, and they are mostly about layout.

  • Paper is 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • The first page has a blank 3 inch margin at the top and at least a half inch on the other sides, with the same half inch margins on later pages.
  • Text is typed or printed in black on white paper, in a font of 9 point or larger.
  • One-sided pages only, with the instrument type stated at the center of the first page.

Blanks may be completed in pen and corrections may be made in pen. A deed prepared by a title attorney's office almost always passes, but a homemade form, a scan with narrow margins or a double-sided print will trigger the surcharge. If you or a family member drafted the deed on a template, check these items before it goes in.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Wake County deed?
sections.html:
The register prints the excise tax on deeds from August 1, 1991 to the present as $2 per thousand dollars. Its recording help page says you may also owe excise tax at the rate of $2 per thousand dollars of the purchase price when you record a deed.

State law writes the same rate as $1.00 on each $500.00 of consideration, and it assigns payment to the transferor before recording. For a sale, that is the seller, and your closing attorney will list the tax on the settlement statement. The amount depends on the price stated in your deed; ask the closing office for the figure on your sale.

Wake County's page also lists older rates, $1 per thousand for 1969 to July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1969. Those matter only for researching an old transfer, not for a sale today.

sections.h2: Which Wake County land records can you search online?
sections.html:
The register runs the Wake County Consolidated Real Property Index, and the county says records are available back to 1785. That gives a seller, or a buyer's attorney, a long chain of title to read from a desk.

Sellers use the index to check that the deed of trust they are paying off appears, and later that the satisfaction has been recorded. The satisfaction itself is free to record, per the county's fee page. Pull your own deed from the same search so the legal description and the spelling of every owner's name match what you will sign at closing.

The office also offers a fraud alert: it can send an email notification when a monitored name is recorded on a document. Owners of rental houses, inherited houses and vacant houses may want to set one up so an unexpected deed does not go unnoticed.

sections.h2: What should you have ready before a Wake County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Have the signed deed, the correct page count and payment ready, and confirm the document meets the standard checklist. A seller working with a closing attorney hands this off, but a seller recording a family transfer or a gift deed may handle it alone.

  • The original signed and acknowledged deed, typed to the margin rules above.
  • Payment for the recording fee, plus excise tax if the transfer is a sale.
  • The names of all parties spelled the way they appear on the prior deed, since the index is searched by name.
  • Any extra instruments that ride in the same document, because each added instrument carries its own $10 charge.

The office records the document you present. A wrong legal description or a missing signature has to be fixed by whoever prepared the deed, and the register suggests an attorney for drafting questions.

sections.h2: Does the Wake County register accept electronic recording?
sections.html:
Ask the office or your closing attorney how a deed will be sent and what cutoff applies. Many closings run electronically, and the attorney will know the process the county uses.

For paper, bring the original signed and acknowledged deed to the Justice Center during office hours, with payment. Call 919-856-5460 for questions about a particular filing. For a name change on title, the register's help page tells visitors that adding or removing a name takes a new deed, and it suggests consulting an attorney unless you are familiar with drafting legal documents.

sections.h2: Why does a deed's recording time matter to a Wake County seller?
sections.html:
In North Carolina a deed does not protect a buyer against lien creditors or other purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Priority among competing instruments follows registration order.

That makes the register the point where a sale becomes effective against the world. A seller who has a deal with a cash buyer should ask the closing attorney to confirm the recording, and should keep the recorded copy with the closing file. If the seller is also carrying an old deed of trust, the lender's satisfaction needs to be recorded too, and recording it costs nothing at the Wake County office.

faqs.q: Is the Wake County Register of Deeds open on Saturdays?
faqs.a: No. The county lists hours as Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., at the Wake County Justice Center in Raleigh. Call 919-856-5460 to check on holidays.

faqs.q: What is the Wake County deed excise tax rate?
faqs.a: The register prints $2 per thousand dollars for deeds from August 1, 1991 to the present. The state statute states it as $1.00 per $500.00, and the seller normally pays it before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does it cost money to record a satisfaction of a deed of trust in Wake County?
faqs.a: No. The register's fee page lists satisfactions of security instruments as free. That includes an affidavit of satisfaction and a trustee's satisfaction of deed of trust.

faqs.q: How do I add or remove a name on a Wake County deed?
faqs.a: Record a new deed. The register says name changes on a deed require a new deed, and it suggests an attorney unless you are familiar with preparing legal documents.

faqs.q: How far back do Wake County deed records go?
faqs.a: The county says its public records go back to 1785 and can be searched online through the Wake County Consolidated Real Property Index.
